name: Jehu
charge: Executing the house of Ahab, then keeping the calves of Jeroboam
summary: Anointed to cut off the house of Ahab, Jehu killed Joram, Ahaziah, Jezebel, seventy sons of Ahab, and every worshipper of Baal in Samaria, and destroyed Baal out of Israel. But from the golden calves at Bethel and Dan Jehu departed not.
offense: Jehu executed the judgment against Ahab's house and destroyed Baal's worship in Israel. Yet he did not depart from Jeroboam's calves at Bethel and Dan (2 Kings 10:28-29). His zeal removed one established evil while leaving another standing. He invited Jehonadab to see his zeal, but the final measure was whether he took heed to walk in the law with all his heart (2 Kings 10:16, 31). A public work of judgment was not a substitute for continuing obedience. The destruction of a rival house did not release the new king from the same commandments.
judgment: The Lord acknowledged what Jehu had done rightly against Ahab and promised that his sons would sit upon Israel's throne to the fourth generation (2 Kings 10:30). The record preserves that reward beside the charge against the calves. Approval of one deed was not blanket approval of the reign. In those days Hazael began cutting Israel short. Jehu's line continued as promised, ending with Zechariah, who was murdered after six months (2 Kings 15:8-12). Hosea also pronounced the visiting of Jezreel's blood upon Jehu's house (Hosea 1:4). The dynasty's promised duration and its eventual reckoning stand together: a commission carried out did not make the house permanent or its bloodshed beyond examination.

entries.commentary: Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him. They submit as his servants, and Jehu's second letter commands them to take the heads of Ahab's seventy sons and bring them to Jezreel by the next day. The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

Jehu meets the brethren of Ahaziah going to salute the king's children and has all forty-two of them slain at the pit of the shearing house, guilty by association with the house of Ahab. He takes up Jehonadab the son of Rechab, whose heart is right with his, into the chariot to see his zeal for the Most High. At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

Jehu gathers all the worshippers of Baal by pretending he will serve Baal much more than Ahab did, doing it in subtilty to destroy them. He fills the house of Baal, brings out vestments for every worshipper, and makes sure no servant of the Most High is among them, only Baal worshippers, as with the clergy garments and idolatry seen in false worship today. After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel. -

Though Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel, he does not depart from the golden calves that Jeroboam set up in Bethel and in Dan; hold Dan in mind for later scriptures. The Most High commends Jehu for executing what is right against the house of Ahab and promises his children to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel. Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin. -

In those days the Most High begins to cut Israel short, and Hazael smites them in all the coasts from Jordan eastward through Gilead and Bashan. The rest of Jehu's acts are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel, and he reigns twenty-eight years in Samaria before Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place. Jehu's life is a warning that the walk is a marathon, not a sprint, and the difference is whether a man gets back up and repents or stays down and departs from the law. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
The word of the Lord came unto Hosea the son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

The Lord tells Hosea to go take a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms, for the land has committed great whoredom, departing from the Lord. He took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, who conceived and bare him a son. He took a whore because it was symbolic of how the people committed spiritual fornication against the Most High.

The Lord tells him to call his name Jezreel, for in a little while he will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu and cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel. At that day he will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.

She conceives again and bears a daughter, named Loruhamah, meaning no more mercy upon the house of Israel, for he will utterly take them away. But he will have mercy upon the house of Judah and save them by the Lord their God, not by bow, nor sword, nor battle, nor horses, nor horsemen.
When she had weaned Loruhamah she conceived and bare a son, named Loammi, meaning ye are not my people and I will not be your God.

Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered, and in the place where it was said they are not my people, there it shall be said they are the sons of the living God. The blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans are the ones whose number is as the sand of the sea, not the so-called white man that calls himself a Jew. The so-called white people as a whole are the minority; they do not reproduce at the rate that other nations do, especially the children of Israel. Because they cannot keep up with the numbers, they come up with tactics to stop other people from reproducing. That is one sign right there that they are not the people of God, for God's people are as the sand of the sea, not the minority.

Then the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, both the northern and southern kingdoms, and appoint themselves one head, and come up out of the land, for great shall be the day of Jezreel. We come together under God's laws and appoint ourselves one head, which is Christ. We do not need any other nation to put a stamp on it, because we already know we are the children of God.

Azariah, also called Uzziah, begins to reign over Judah and does that which is right in the sight of the Most High as his father Amaziah had done. The high places were not removed, so the people still sacrificed and burned incense there, an incomplete obedience. The Most High smote him so that he was a leper until his death, and he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people. Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to [2 Chronicles 26](/bible/2-chronicles/26) for a more detailed account of his life and acts. -

Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel only six months and does that which is evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Shallum conspires against Zachariah, smites him before the people, slays him, and reigns in his place. The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation. -

Shallum reigns a full month in Samaria before Menahem son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah, smites him, and reigns in his stead. Menahem strikes Tiphsah and its coasts because they would not open to him, and he ripped up the women with child, a mark of his cruelty.

Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand. Menahem raises the tribute by exacting fifty shekels of silver from each mighty man of wealth, so the king of Assyria turns back and does not stay in the land.

Pekahiah son of Menahem reigns two years over Israel and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pekah, a captain of his, conspires against him and smites him in the king's house at Samaria with fifty Gileadites, then reigns in his room. This is a military coup, where a trusted captain kills the king and seizes the throne.

Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years over Israel, the same Pekah spoken of in the book of Isaiah. In his days Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and takes Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, carrying them captive to Assyria. Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, smites and slays him, and reigns in his stead.

Jotham son of Uzziah reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem and does that which is right, according to all his father Uzziah had done. Again the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. Jotham builds the higher gate of the house of the Most High. In those days the Most High begins to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

verses.text: And he arose, and went into the house; and he poured the oil on his head, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed thee king over the people of the Lord, even over Israel.
And thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the Lord, at the hand of Jezebel.
For the whole house of Ahab shall perish: and I will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel:
And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah:
And the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her. And he opened the door, and fled.
So Jehu slew all that remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, and his kinsfolks, and his priests, until he left him none remaining.
Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
Howbeit from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, Jehu departed not from after them, to wit, the golden calves that were in Beth–el, and that were in Dan.

And the Lord said unto Jehu, Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.
But Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart: for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, which made Israel to sin.
In those days the Lord began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel;
From Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
And the Lord said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah did Zachariah the son of Jeroboam reign over Israel in Samaria six months.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his fathers had done: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
And the rest of the acts of Zachariah, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
This was the word of the Lord which he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
Obedience to God required by walking in His ways and by keeping His commandments.
Civil rulers are to record, preserve, study and proclaim the law of God at all times.
Do not be hypocritical in serving God or in living a godly life.
